money.body: Sells you an outcome and skips the skill. When the trend moves on, you're left with a course and no habit.

fluff.body: Explains the technology without touching your work. You leave informed and exactly as slow as you arrived.

irl.body: Twelve weeks standard, adjusted to the group. One-off workshops through long-form programs. Taught by people who run their own work on these tools.

custom.title: Your own curriculum
custom.body: Being built now: a curriculum that teaches you to learn with your assistant, whichever one you use. Setup, how to ask, cost control, a library of tools and repos with plain explanations, memory and knowledge graphs, all built from what we learn about you. story.headline: Why we started this
story.body: In 2019 a friend at OpenAI got me into an early API program, a year before ChatGPT existed. I've built with AI every day since. Friends started asking me to set up their systems. They got 10+ hours a week back, and they all said the same thing: you should teach this. So we did.

platform.headline: AI changes daily. Keeping up is a job.
platform.body: New models, new tools, a dozen papers before lunch. It's hard to follow even for us, and following it is our work. So we built the place where you don't have to do it alone.

structure.headline: How the twelve weeks run
structure.body: Three blocks of four weeks: Foundations, Build, Deepen and capstone. Each block can be booked on its own.

blocks.title: Weeks 1 to 3, the spine
blocks.line: How these systems work: pipelines, agents, memory, harnesses, the compound loop. Your tools set up. A map of your own week, and the three tasks worth automating first.

blocks.title: Weeks 4 to 10, your track
blocks.line: Seven weeks on the work your track is made of. Weeks 4 and 5 go deep on the track's highest-value workflow. Week 9 is verification: catching what the assistant got wrong. Week 10 draws your personal system map and plans the capstone.

blocks.title: Weeks 11 to 12, capstone
blocks.line: One fully running system on your real job. The same task before and after, with the artifacts to prove it. Then a handoff into the platform.

week.headline: How a session runs
week.body: Two hours, once a week, the same shape every time, so nobody has to learn the class, only the content.

rules: At least half of every session is you building on your own material, from a template, never from a blank page.
The demo shows the usual way failing in front of the room before it shows the method.
The assignment is real work, logged: a task from your job done the new way, with time and output recorded. Those logs are your before and after.
Your work is yours. Nobody sees it unless you choose, and confidential material never goes into a tool in the room.

items.title: Browser-only
items.line: Every track. Your assistant in the browser, your company's own suite, nothing installed. The path for corporate IT that blocks everything else.

measure.headline: Measured, not felt
measure.body: You log a baseline in week one. In week twelve you show the same task before and after: both outputs, both durations, one quality checklist. Nobody graduates on "I feel faster."

items.q: Do I need to know how to code?
items.a: No. Most people we teach don't. If you do, you'll move faster on the agent path.
Yes. Your own, with a working login to whichever assistant your company permits. A checklist arrives a week before session one so setup is done before you sit down.

items.q: Which AI tools do you teach?
items.a: Whichever assistant your company permits: ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini are interchangeable for every exercise. The method is the content; the tool picks are dated and listed with the reason for each.
Tool cost is $0 to $20 a month on the browser path, more on the agent path. Course prices are published soon; ask us in the meantime.

items.q: Can I book one block instead of twelve weeks?
items.a: Yes. Foundations, Build, and Deepen and capstone are four weeks each and can be booked alone.

items.q: Can my company book a cohort?
items.a: Yes. Corporate training has its own page and its own form. The browser-only path exists for exactly the IT rules most companies have.
Twelve, with a parent's okay. The student course is in development; join the waitlist and we'll tell you when it opens.

paragraphs: In 2019 a friend at OpenAI got me into an early API program. ChatGPT didn't exist yet. The models were strange and expensive, and I built with them every day anyway, because it was obvious something had changed.

A few years in, friends started asking me to set up their systems. Not to explain AI. To make it do their work. I'd sit with them for an afternoon, and they'd get ten or more hours a week back. Every one of them said the same thing afterward: you should teach this.
One of them did more than say it. Twenty years in emerging tech, a system I had set up, and the decision to turn a favor into a company. That is the co-founder.
So we teach what we use. We measure in hours and output. We tell you when we don't know. Everything here is an experiment, and that is what the asterisk means.
